findings.evidence: template/scripts/requirement_board.py:58-61 calls observe() for the Done guard, then reconcile_nonterminal (lines 31 and 38) runs aggregate() and observe() again. The Done guard could reuse the observation or sit inside reconcile_nonterminal. This is not a correctness defect.
findings.summary: claim_started observes the card, then reconcile_nonterminal runs a full requirement_intake.aggregate and observes the card again. Every start and advance entry pays for these extra GitHub reads, and the claim sits in the window the change is meant to shorten.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/execute_requirement.py:217 calls claim_started before orchestrate_pre_authoring.status (line 218). The 'has started and its state is kept' wording in requirement_board.py:63-66 is shared by both call sites, including advance.
findings.summary: advance claims the card without checking that pre-authoring state exists. On a Requirement that was never started, advance can move the card to In progress and only afterwards fail in orchestrate_pre_authoring.status. The error text then says the Requirement 'has started and its state is kept', which would be false.
